item.title: Windows PE Format
item.description:
Portable Executable (PE) is the executable-image format used by Windows and by UEFI PE/COFF images. Unlike ELF, PE has no program-header table. The loader maps the image from the COFF header, optional header, section table, and data directories.

File Layout #

A PE image starts with a DOS header (MZ). Its e_lfanew member points to the NT headers, which begin with the PE\0\0 signature. A DOS stub follows the DOS header; some toolchains also emit a non-standard Rich header before the NT headers.

item.title: PowerShell Splatting and Hashtable Values
item.description:
PowerShell splatting passes a hashtable or array as named or positional arguments. It avoids repeating long parameter lists and keeps configuration separate from a command invocation.

Splatting PowerShell Commands #

Prefix a hashtable variable with @ at the call site:

powershell 
$request = @{
 Uri = 'https://api.example.test/items'
 Method = 'Get'
 Headers = @{ Accept = 'application/json' }
 TimeoutSec = 30
}

Invoke-RestMethod @request

Hashtable keys must match parameter names, including supported aliases. Splatting does not expand arbitrary strings into shell syntax; PowerShell binds the resulting values as typed command arguments.
